positionKey.In-line: A = lower panel, B = taller panel, in line (180°).
positionKey.L: A = lower panel, B = taller panel, meeting at 90°. Ships right-handed.
positionKey.T: A and C = the two collinear run panels (straight bar of the T, on opposite sides of the junction); B = the perpendicular stem at 90°. Handed (right) when A ≠ C.
positionKey.X: Four panels at 90°: A and C collinear (one run), B and D collinear (crossing run); order around the junction A, B, C, D (A front-left, B front-right, C back-right, D back-left in the diagrams).
positionKey.V: A = lower panel, B = taller panel, meeting at 120°. Ships right-handed.
positionKey.Y: Three panels at 120°: A = the leg whose height differs; B and C = the other two (equal-height) legs.

rules.text: Thin base junctions (in-line, L, T, X, end-of-run, V, Y) are offered in 30", 42", 48", 54", 66" and 78" panel heights. The statement of line also dots wall-start at 30", but wall-start junctions are not available at 30" (28 7/16") per p14 note and p24; spec page 359 lists 42"-78" only.
Change-of-height junctions exist for in-line, L, T, X, V and Y configurations; they accommodate most panel heights and combinations (see visual overview pp20-23).

Stacking junctions are available in 12", 18" and 24" heights for in-line, L, T, X, end-of-run, V, Y and wall-start configurations (plus a 36" end-of-run stacker used only in build-your-own change-of-height, p362).
Thin, square and oval trim styles are not compatible with each other. Applications must use one consistent trim style.
Stacking horizontal frame package must be used with stacking junctions (p382).
Stacking junctions do not come with trim; vertical trim must be ordered separately to cover any exposed junctions.
Base junctions are always shared by adjacent panels. Wall-start junctions and off-module connectors are also available.
Leveling glides adjust to install panels on uneven floors; range is 2 3/4".

Alternate powerkit harness routing can be accommodated through the junction opening. In in-line applications installed on uneven floors, route harness through junction opening to prevent harness from being exposed.
Junctions determine panel height and horizontal connecting bars determine width; plan frames first.
Corner junctions can be reconfigured by adding or removing a junction post (available on junctions shipped on or after October 10, 2011).
Thin trim requires end-of-run and change-of-height junctions manufactured on or after October 10, 2011.
Base junctions are specified with desired trim style; styles cannot be mixed between adjacent panels.

Slots in junction accept the panel's horizontal bars every 12", cable trays every 6", and powerkits every 12" vertically. Slotted channels accommodate worksurface supports and overhead storage components at 1" increments.

Trim is included with L, T, V and end-of-run junctions to finish exposed surfaces; trim is available in paint or wood veneer. Junction cap and appropriate aligners are included with the junction when needed.
Inside corner light seals are only needed in 90° applications and are included in the style number when ordering.
End-of-run base junction includes junction, vertical trim and trim aligner; end-of-run trim adds 1/2" to footprint.
In-line base junction includes junction and plastic top cap aligner.
Large openings route power or cables through L, T, X, V, Y and in-line base junctions; lay-in cable routing through opening in top of junction beneath top caps and in base area.
Wall-start junctions are not available in the 28 7/16" (30" nominal) height.
L same height base junction includes junction, inside corner light seal(s), vertical trim, junction cap and two plastic top cap aligners.
T same height base junction includes junction, inside corner light seal(s), vertical trim, junction cap and three plastic top cap aligners.
X same height base junction includes junction, inside corner light seal(s), junction cap and four plastic top cap aligners.
V same height base junction includes junction, vertical trim, junction cap and plastic top cap aligner.
Y same height base junction includes junction, junction cap and two plastic top cap aligners.
Wall-start junction secures to the stud in a structural wall (or drywall fasteners can be used); vertical trim is not needed; also used in off-module applications; adds 3/16" dimension to panel run.
An in-line top cap aligner is included with in-line junctions; top cap aligners are included with end-of-run, L, T, X, V and Y junctions.
Block and post construction of corner junctions allows posts to be added or removed to configure between L, T, X, V or Y.
Floor anchor brackets secure junctions to the floor to prevent panel movement; intended for seismic zones and may require additional code approvals. Floor anchor bolts are not included (p360).

Junction stabilizer bracket adds rigidity to a panel run or is used with a Universal sliding door; must be bolted to a concrete floor. Use TS7SB for junctions manufactured before October 10, 2011 and TS7SBNJ for junctions manufactured on or after October 10, 2011.

Junction stabilizer bracket blocks power routing in the panel base and just above the base (covers powerkit slots in these zones; blocks powerkit harness, pass-through powerkit or modular harness routing in the base from an adjacent panel) and blocks lay-in of cables in the base area. Bracket foot is visible on one side of the panel.

Base junctions can accept a stacking junction. Omit trim option should be selected whenever stacking; omitting trim removes all vertical trim, junction cap and aligner(s) — specify vertical trim, junction cap, inside corner light seal(s) and aligners separately (p373).
Most change-of-height junction configurations are pre-configured and include junctions and needed trims; configurations not pre-configured are available through build your own (p373).
Painted style numbers include all painted trim and wood style numbers include all wood trim. Mixing painted and wood trim is not recommended (wood trim is slightly thicker; misalignment may result).

Answer panel wood trims are only available with quarter-cut finishes except maple, which is only flat-cut. Either may be specified; non-maple flat-cut selections get the coordinating quarter-cut, maple quarter-cut selections get flat-cut.
Junction tall sleeves and carpet gripper glide caps can only be used on junctions manufactured on or after October 10, 2011.
Stacking junctions can be used with any height base junction.
Modular harnesses 43" or 80" are available to change the height at which power kits are routed.
See Stability Guidelines, page 124, for application rules.
Change-of-height trims are available in 12"H, 18"H, 24"H, 30"H and 36"H.

Two-height L, T, X, V and Y change-of-height junctions are supported by style numbers. Three-height T, X and Y and four-height X junctions are NOT supported by style numbers and must be specified via build your own (pp28-43).
Change-of-height junctions include the necessary change-of-height trim (including junction cap and aligners) for the change-of-height portion.

Change-of-height junctions are shipped assembled. L, V and some T junctions are handed (shipped right-handed); a post may have to be moved during installation to achieve the proper hand. The other hand is not supported by style numbers.

An end-of-run aligner is included with the end-of-run change-of-height trim; no junction cap is required. End-of-run change-of-height trim is used at end-of-run or in-line change-of-height; its top aligns with the top cap.

L corner change-of-height trim is used in a T or X change-of-height application when two panels at the tallest height are adjacent to each other; no aligners required to connect it to the junction cap.
An L to T aligner must be specified when an L corner change-of-height trim resides directly above a T trim.
T corner change-of-height trim is used in T or X change-of-height applications where two panels at the same height are located in-line with each other; no aligners required.

120° corner change-of-height trim is used in a V or Y change-of-height application when only one panel is at the tallest height; no aligners required. A 120° to V aligner should be specified when a 120° corner change-of-height trim resides directly above a V trim.
V corner change-of-height trim is used in a Y change-of-height application when two panels are at the tallest height; no aligners required.

Change-of-height top cap option must be specified on the lower panel of in-line applications; it is only needed with in-line change-of-height. Specify change-of-height top caps at one end unless the panel is adjacent to taller panels on both sides, then specify change-of-height on both ends.
In-line change-of-height junction (e.g. 42"/66") includes a 42" in-line base junction with a 24" end-of-run stacker; a horizontal stacking beam is required to support the stacker.
When using frameless glass in a change-of-height application going from 48"H to 66"H, it must be stacked at the transition point above the 48" height.
Change-of-height trim and junction cap: paint or wood veneer. Aligner: black plastic only.

Style numbers for change-of-height junctions are built from single height digits: 3=30", 4=42", 8=48", 5=54", 6=66", 7=78", 9=90"; digits appear in diagram position order (A,B[,C[,D]]). Style numbers for wood junctions require a W at the end.
All same height corner junctions are on pages 345-348; if the application needs three heights in a T, X or Y or four heights in an X, use Build Your Own—Thin Trim (p33).
T change-of-height junctions are handed (ship right-handed) when A and C are different heights; A = C T junctions are not handed.
Off-module panel connectors attach a fin wall off-module to a spine wall in 1" increments.
Wall-start junction must be ordered separately; available 42"H, 48"H, 54"H, 66"H and 78"H and must match the height of the fin wall.
Bottom channel has slots in 1" increments; channel must match width of panel and be attached between two junctions.
Off-module fin wall must always be the same height or shorter than the spine wall.

If fin wall is 12", 18" or 24" shorter than the spine wall, the top horizontal connecting bar can be lowered to attach brackets (24" maximum). When the fin wall is more than 24" shorter than the spine wall, an additional horizontal beam must be added to the spine at the fin-wall height — order a stacking horizontal frame kit — and spine skins must be segmented with a seam matching the fin wall height.
An off-module fin wall cannot connect flush to the end of a spine panel; the closest connection leaves a 2 1/2" tail on the spine including end-of-run trim.
An off-module fin wall cannot attach at a junction in the spine wall: 2" of dead space on either side of the junction (4" total).
When using frameless glass on a spine panel with same height off-module panel connections, the off-module panel cannot connect within 10" of an end-of-run or in-line junction connection.
Two off-module panels can be connected back to back at the same location.
When attaching a 48"H panel to a 66"H panel off-module, the 66"H must be a 48"H base with an 18"H stacker.

When stacking wall-start junctions in an off-module application, the off-module panel connector connects to the base wall-start junction. When stacking on the fin panel, spine wall skins must be segmented with a seam matching the height of the fin base panel.
When connecting two off-module fins at different heights on either side of the spine, an additional horizontal beam must be ordered and installed at the height of the shorter fin.

An off-module fin wall cannot be installed over a window located at the top of a spine panel. Bins, shelves and worksurfaces cannot be attached off-module. Off-module installation requires field modification of the light seal on the top skin.

Wiring and cabling cannot be routed internally from a spine wall to an off-module fin wall without cutting openings in the spine wall skin; route through the spine wall and use internode power components.

Pre-Oct-10-2011 wall-start junction with a post-Oct-10-2011 off-module connector: the 'old' bottom bracket must be used (Service Parts TS500938MP per p25; p361 prints T500938MP). Old (pre-Oct-10-2011) off-module connector with a new wall-start junction: use the bottom bracket included with the connector. Wall-start junctions made before October 2002 will not work with off-module connectors (p361).
Off-module panel connector works with thin trims; thin (and square) trims do not require the top cap filler (filler is for oval only, p361).
All existing base panels can accept a stacking junction. Same height stacking corner junction posts and block come plant assembled in a designated L, T, X, V or Y configuration.
Stacking horizontal frame package (specified separately) must be used with stacking junctions; each package includes one horizontal connecting bar.

When stacking, omit base junction trim and specify full height (base height plus stacking height) vertical trim, inside corner light seal(s) (90° applications only), junction cap and aligners separately.
Base panel must always have two horizontal connecting bars in place prior to adding fork connectors into the junction.
End-of-run stacking junction includes junction and fork connector; full height trim must be specified separately; end-of-run trim adds 1/2" to footprint.
Fork connectors included: two with in-line, L and V stacking junctions; three with T and Y; four with X; one with each wall-start and end-of-run stacking junction.
Stacking L, T, V, X, Y junctions: full height trim, inside corner light seal(s), junction cap and aligner(s) must be specified separately.

Maximum height that can be stacked on a base panel is 36", consisting of one 24"H and one 12"H, or two 18"H stacking junctions. Maximum number of stacking junctions on a base panel is two. Maximum height an Answer panel configuration can reach is 90".
Any height base panel can be used with stacking junctions.
Bins and shelves can hang from the first stacked tier only.
Consolidation point kit cannot be used with stacking components.
Full height vertical trim is available in build your own in 42", 48", 54", 60", 66", 72", 78", 84" and 90" (pp367-369).
Junction tall sleeves (cover exposed metal edges in large cable routing opening) only for junctions manufactured on or after October 10, 2011.

Standard skins, cable trays and powerkits are used in stackable solutions; consider matching skin height to stacking junction height. Skins on the base panel usually need not be removed to install a stacking junction.
36" end-of-run stacker (TS736TEPJS) is only used in build-your-own change-of-height applications and must never be used as an end-of-run stacking junction.
Stacking corner junctions do not include trim or junction cap; junction cap must be specified separately.
Stacking in-line junctions do not require junction cap and trim.
In-line base panel junctions do not require junction cap and trim.
When omit trim is selected on base junctions (used when stacking), specify vertical trim separately to span full base + stacking junction height, and specify junction cap and aligners.
Specify a stacking horizontal frame package with an in-line change-of-height junction, unless there is a window in the top position of the taller panel.

Omit trim on change-of-height junctions omits all vertical and change-of-height trim (used when stacking on base junctions); vertical and change-of-height trim then must be specified separately to span the full height of the base junction plus stacking junction, plus junction caps and aligners.
When a wall-start junction is used in an off-module application, the off-module panel connector must be ordered separately.
Off-module panel connectors must be used with wall-start junctions, ordered separately.

TS7TJUP works with L, T or X base junctions of any height and T or X change-of-height junctions as long as at least two panels are at the tallest height; otherwise a square trim junction utility pole may be used (adds 3" of dimension, p410).

TS7TJUP cannot be used with L change-of-height junctions and can only be used with junctions manufactured on or after October 10, 2011. Junction not included (order separately). Order multipurpose power infeed separately (p483).
Order multipurpose power infeed separately for lay-in utility packages (p483).
30"W floor-access lay-in utility package is only available with change-of-height top cap at one end; change-of-height at both ends is offered only on 36"-48"W packages.

Junctions manufactured before 10/10/11 (purpose built): skin clip attachment every 12"; cannot accept 6" technology skin; cannot accept open base trim; large power/data opening only at worksurface height; corner junctions cannot change configuration.

Junctions manufactured after 10/10/11 (universal): skin clip attachment every 6"; accept 6" technology skin; accept open base trim; large openings every 12"; corner junctions can be transformed (e.g. L to T). Purpose built and universal corner junctions can be used in the same application.
In-line junctions manufactured before or after 10/10/11 can be used with Thin trim; in-line junctions work with Oval, Square or Thin trim.
Same height corner junctions are interchangeable between Oval, Square and Thin trim; those manufactured before or after 10/10/11 can be used with Thin trim.

Universal junction reconfiguration: L→T add one post, replace L trim with T trim, add a junction cap aligner (inventory L trim); L→X add one post, add two junction cap aligners (inventory L trim); T→L remove one post, remove one aligner, replace T trim with L trim; X→L remove two posts, remove two aligners, add an L trim; X→T remove one post, remove one aligner, add a T trim.
Purpose built (pre-10/10/11) corner junctions cannot be reconfigured; to change L to T the entire junction must be changed out.

Thin change-of-height corner junctions can only use universal junctions manufactured after 10/10/11; cannot accept purpose built change-of-height junctions made before 10/10/11. Junction posts only go up to the height of each panel (e.g. 42/54 L: one post at 42"H, one at 54"H).
When reconfiguring from Square or Oval trim to Thin trim, purpose built corner junctions must be changed to universal corner junctions.

Thin trim requires Thin end-of-run junctions; when reconfiguring from Square/Oval to Thin all end-of-run junctions must be changed to Thin end-of-run junctions. Square/Oval applications use the in-line junction at end-of-run and cannot use Thin end-of-run junctions.
Stacking junctions manufactured before or after 10/10/11 can be stacked on either purpose built (pre-10/10/11) or universal (post-10/10/11) junctions.
Trim style must be consistent across the entire application (e.g. square top caps cannot be used with thin vertical trims).

An end-of-run junction post can be re-used at an end-of-run or as a post in a 90° or 120° corner. In-line junctions cannot be used at an end-of-run with Thin trim (can with Square or Oval) and cannot be used at a corner junction. When reconfiguring corner junctions, additional corner trim and aligner pieces must be ordered.
Before 10/10/11 Oval and Square junctions were purpose built; from 10/10/11 they are universal with the same style numbers. SmartTools designates old junctions with an asterisk.
